draft.title: Compass and true bearings
card: It starts from north or south, then turns east or west by an angle. S40°E means start facing south, then turn 40° towards east.
It is measured clockwise from north and written with three digits. East is 090°, south is 180° and west is 270°.
S40°E is 40° east of south. South is 180°, and turning towards east takes you back round to 140°. So S40°E is 140°.
N30°W is 30° west of north. Going anticlockwise from north gives \(360^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 330^{\circ}\). So N30°W is the true bearing 330°.
draft.remember: True bearings go clockwise from north in three digits. Compass bearings start from north or south.

a.q: What is the true bearing for the compass bearing S40°E?
a.why: South is 180°. Turning 40° towards east means going back 40° from 180°, which gives 140°. 220° is wrong because it turns towards west instead.
a.clue: South is 180°. Is east before or after south going clockwise from north?

b.q: A hiker in the Blue Mountains walks on a true bearing of 250°. What is this as a compass bearing?
b.why: 250° is between 180° (south) and 270° (west), so the direction is south-west. It is \(250^{\circ} - 180^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}\) past south towards west, so S70°W. S20°W is wrong because 20° is the angle from west, not from south.
b.clue: Which quarter is 250° in, and how far is it from south?

wants.brief: A compass rose with north at the top. A point at the centre with a ray pointing south-east, marked with the 40° angle from south towards east, labelled S40°E. A curved clockwise arrow from north round to the ray, labelled 140°.
wants.why: It shows the same direction as a compass bearing and as a true bearing.

check.summary: No problems found. The conversions are all correct: S40°E is 140°, N30°W is 330° and 250° is S70°W.
